output.title: Deadline for a Prescriber to Schedule a Peer-to-Peer Review After a Denial
output.draft_text:
Question: How many days does a prescriber have to schedule a peer-to-peer review after a denial?

Answer: After a prior authorization or coverage request is denied, the prescriber has [number of days] [calendar or business] days from [starting event, e.g., the date of the denial notice] to request a peer-to-peer review.

How the prescriber schedules it: The prescriber or their office contacts [department or team name] at [phone number / fax / portal] and provides [required information, e.g., member ID, case or reference number, drug name]. Only [who may request, e.g., the prescribing provider or authorized office staff] can request the review.

What happens after the window closes: If the peer-to-peer window has passed, [next available option, e.g., the prescriber or member may submit a formal appeal or a new request]. The deadline for that option is [appeal deadline].

What advocates can tell the member: The advocate can tell the member the denial date, the peer-to-peer deadline, and how the prescriber can schedule the review. Advocates [can / cannot] schedule a peer-to-peer on the prescriber's behalf.

Exceptions: [Any differences by plan type, line of business, state, or urgent/expedited requests, or 'None'].

author_checklist: Confirm the number of days a prescriber has to request a peer-to-peer review after a denial, using the governing policy or contract.
Confirm whether the window is counted in calendar days or business days.
Confirm the event that starts the window, such as the denial decision date, the notice date, or the date the notice is received.
Confirm the contact method and department for scheduling, including phone, fax, or portal details.
Confirm who is allowed to request a peer-to-peer review.
Confirm what information the prescriber must provide when requesting.
Confirm what options are available after the peer-to-peer window expires, and confirm the appeal deadlines.
Confirm whether advocates may schedule or initiate a peer-to-peer on the prescriber's behalf.
Confirm whether the deadline varies by plan type, line of business, state regulation, or for expedited/urgent cases.
Cite the source policy document and effective date before submitting for approval.
